  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Nevertheless, there is an advantage specifically in miracles clothed in nature, and the difference between the two types of miracles parallels the difference between the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">However, nevertheless, there is also an advantage in miracles that are clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="1">for specifically in these miracles, the dominion of Ein Sof over</t>
    <t s="2">(the manner of)</t>
    <t s="3">nature itself is revealed.</t>
    <t s="4">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that the difference between the two types of miracles is analogous to the difference between the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol.</t>
    <t s="6">For this, that with regard to the revelation of Ein Sof, blessed be He, nature is nullified from its existence</t>
    <t s="7">(miracles that are above nature)</t>
    <t s="8">is analogous to the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah</t>
    <t s="9">(bittul in existence)</t>
    <t s="10">which comes through the contemplation that everything before Him is considered as nothing,</t>
    <t s="11">And this, that nature remains in its existence and nevertheless the manner of its conduct is</t>
    <t s="12">(not according to the laws and properties of nature,</t>
    <t s="13">but rather)</t>
    <t s="14">according to His will, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="15">(miracles clothed in nature)</t>
    <t s="16">is analogous to the bittul of Kabbalas Ol,</t>
    <t s="17">for although he remains in his existence, and even [to the extent that] "a servant prefers to be free,"</t>
    <t s="18">nevertheless, his actual conduct is not according to his own will but according to the will of the Master.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The advantage of bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah is that it encompasses one's entire existence, while the advantage of bittul of Kabbalas Ol is that it is a true bittul, not contingent on one's self-awareness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known,</t>
    <t s="2">that the advantage in the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah is that the bittul is in his entire existence</t>
    <t s="3">(so that there remains in him and with him no matter that is not nullified,</t>
    <t s="4">and unlike the bittul of Kabbalas Ol, where the bittul is only regarding actual deed),</t>
    <t s="5">and the advantage in the bittul of Kabbalas Ol is in the bittul itself,</t>
    <t s="6">that it is a true bittul, not connected to the existence of the person.</t>
    <t s="7">For the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah,</t>
    <t s="8">since the bittul is through one recognizing and feeling that everything before Him is considered as nothing,</t>
    <t s="9">the bittul is connected to the existence of the person</t>
    <t s="10">(his cognition)</t>
    <t s="11">and is not a true bittul,</t>
    <t s="12">and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol,</t>
    <t s="13">where one accepts upon himself to fulfill the command of G-d even when the command is against his will,</t>
    <t s="14">in the manner of a servant who is compelled to fulfill the will of the Master,</t>
    <t s="15">since the essence of this bittul is not to take his own existence into account,</t>
    <t s="16">this is a true bittul.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly, in miracles clothed in nature, although nature's existence is not nullified, the change in its conduct is a true bittul because it stems from Ein Sof's dominion over nature.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said that this is analogous regarding miracles clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="1">for although the bittul of nature to Ein Sof in these miracles is only regarding the manner of nature's conduct and not regarding its essential existence,</t>
    <t s="2">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="3">since from the perspective of the laws and properties of nature there is no place for the conduct of nature to be in a miraculous manner,</t>
    <t s="4">and the change</t>
    <t s="5">(the miracle)</t>
    <t s="6">that is made in the conduct of nature is because Ein Sof rules over nature and conducts nature according to His will,</t>
    <t s="7">the bittul of nature in these miracles is a true bittul.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Nevertheless, there is an advantage specifically in miracles clothed in nature, and the difference between the two types of miracles parallels the difference between the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol.

translations.translation: However, nevertheless, there is also an advantage in miracles that are clothed in nature,
for specifically in these miracles, the dominion of Ein Sof over
(the manner of)
nature itself is revealed.
And it can be said,
that the difference between the two types of miracles is analogous to the difference between the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol.
For this, that with regard to the revelation of Ein Sof, blessed be He, nature is nullified from its existence
(miracles that are above nature)
is analogous to the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah
(bittul in existence)
which comes through the contemplation that everything before Him is considered as nothing,
And this, that nature remains in its existence and nevertheless the manner of its conduct is
(not according to the laws and properties of nature,
but rather)
according to His will, blessed be He
(miracles clothed in nature)
is analogous to the bittul of Kabbalas Ol,
for although he remains in his existence, and even [to the extent that] "a servant prefers to be free,"
nevertheless, his actual conduct is not according to his own will but according to the will of the Master.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The advantage of bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah is that it encompasses one's entire existence, while the advantage of bittul of Kabbalas Ol is that it is a true bittul, not contingent on one's self-awareness.

translations.translation: And it is known,
that the advantage in the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah is that the bittul is in his entire existence
(so that there remains in him and with him no matter that is not nullified,
and unlike the bittul of Kabbalas Ol, where the bittul is only regarding actual deed),
and the advantage in the bittul of Kabbalas Ol is in the bittul itself,
that it is a true bittul, not connected to the existence of the person.
For the bittul of Yichuda Ila'ah,
since the bittul is through one recognizing and feeling that everything before Him is considered as nothing,
the bittul is connected to the existence of the person
(his cognition)
and is not a true bittul,
and the bittul of Kabbalas Ol,
where one accepts upon himself to fulfill the command of G-d even when the command is against his will,
in the manner of a servant who is compelled to fulfill the will of the Master,
since the essence of this bittul is not to take his own existence into account,
this is a true bittul.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Similarly, in miracles clothed in nature, although nature's existence is not nullified, the change in its conduct is a true bittul because it stems from Ein Sof's dominion over nature.

translations.translation: And it can be said that this is analogous regarding miracles clothed in nature,
for although the bittul of nature to Ein Sof in these miracles is only regarding the manner of nature's conduct and not regarding its essential existence,
nevertheless,
since from the perspective of the laws and properties of nature there is no place for the conduct of nature to be in a miraculous manner,
and the change
(the miracle)
that is made in the conduct of nature is because Ein Sof rules over nature and conducts nature according to His will,
the bittul of nature in these miracles is a true bittul.
